title: South Africa first, then Kenya's Wild Loop
overview:
- **Dates:** LAX **Sat Dec 19** → South Africa → Nairobi → LAX **Sat Jan 16**. Christmas in South Africa; Kenya from Dec 28 is the Wild loop unchanged.
- **Stopover:** 3 nights on the Cape Peninsula (penguins, fynbos, Table Mountain), then 3 nights self-driving in southern Kruger in SANParks rest camps. Christmas is in Kruger. On Dec 27 you exit via Nelspruit (MQP) and reach NBO at 22:05.
- **Verdict:** This is the most varied and self-sufficient stopover. The Cape adds wildlife and scenery Kenya doesn't have (penguins, fur seals, fynbos), and Kruger adds rhino, wild dog and leopard on cheap self-drive. It is also the most expensive stopover: about +$2,400 pp over the base trip, driven by 3 extra regional flights at peak fares. Kruger also partly duplicates the 19-night Kenya safari, and December school holidays mean SANParks camps may already be full, so check availability before buying anything. Checked: (1) TK44's winter departure is 01:55, not 01:45, so the IST layover is about 7h. (2) The Dec 27 exit is reworked. Skukuza-JNB flights leave only at about 13:35 or 14:35, which gave a dangerously short connection to KQ763 at 17:00 on a separate ticket. The plan now drives Lower Sabie to Kruger Mpumalanga airport (MQP, about 2.5h) for the 10:50 Airlink flight to JNB, leaving a 5h+ buffer. (3) The KQ763 fare is raised to about $450 (recent one-way fares about $410-450). A one-way car drop fee is added. (4) The headline delta is corrected from +$2,000 to about +$2,400, because the line items already summed to more than +$2,000. (5) Kidnapping and terrorism are added to the advisory notes. KQ763 (17:00 to 22:05), TK44's arrival, Airlink 4Z651 (10:30), the R602 conservation fee and the Level 2 advisory were all confirmed.
- **Safety:** US State Dept Level 2: Exercise Increased Caution (issued May 27 2025, still Level 2 per reports as of Mar 2026; re-check travel.state.gov). The advisory cites crime, terrorism, unrest and kidnapping. In practice the main risk for tourists is violent crime (robbery, carjacking, smash-and-grab, mugging) in city centers, at traffic lights and on some highways after dark. The places on this route (Gardens/City Bowl, the Cape Peninsula drive, Kruger camps, the N4 to Nelspruit in daylight, airports) are routine for tourists and low risk if you follow the usual precautions. Inside Kruger the main hazards are wildlife, speeding and heat, not crime. Southern Kruger is a low-to-moderate malaria area in summer.
- **Cost:** $9,980 pp, **+$2,380** vs the Wild loop alone ($7,600).

**Highlights:** African penguin colony at Boulders Beach (boardwalks, near-certain sightings) · Cape Point / Cape of Good Hope: fynbos, bontebok, eland, baboons, ostriches, dramatic cliffs · Chapman's Peak Drive and Table Mountain cableway with views of the whole peninsula · Kirstenbosch Botanical Garden: proteas and Cape sugarbirds · Southern Kruger 'Big 5' self-drive: H4-1 Sabie River road and H4-2 / S28 around Lower Sabie, among the park's best areas for rhino, leopard, lion and wild dog · SANParks guided sunset or night drive (the only way to see nocturnal animals inside Kruger) · Christmas at Lower Sabie with hippos and elephants on the Sabie River below the deck · Two biomes Kenya doesn't have: the Cape Floral Kingdom and the marine side of the Cape

**Drawbacks:** Most expensive option: about +$2,400 pp all-in over the $1,500 base, mainly because of 3 regional flights (CPT-SZK, MQP-JNB, JNB-NBO) bought at Christmas prices. · Kruger is another savanna safari right before 19 nights of Kenyan safari, so expect some 'more of the same'. Rhino and wild dog are the main extras. · Peak season plus South African school holidays: SANParks camps, Airlink seats and rental cars sell out. Skukuza and Lower Sabie may already be full. The fallback is to stay just outside the park (Marloth Park, Komatipoort or Hazyview guesthouses, about R1,400-2,000 per room), with longer drives. · Dec 27 is a long day: about 2.5h of road to MQP, a 1h flight, about 5h of waiting at JNB, then KQ763 landing NBO at 22:05. The Dec 28 Nairobi rest day absorbs it. · Skukuza's own flights to JNB (4Z862 about 13:35, 4Z866 about 14:35) arrive too late for a safe self-transfer to KQ763 at 17:00, which is why the plan exits via MQP. Airlink and KQ are separate tickets, so there is no protection if you misconnect. · Cheaper variant (about +$1,300 pp instead of +$2,400): Kruger only. Fly TK into JNB, rent a car, rest a night at the airport, drive 4.5h to Malelane gate, spend 4 nights in Kruger, drive back, then KQ763. It skips the Cape and has two 5h drive days. · Pricier upgrade: 2 nights at a private Sabi Sand or Timbavati lodge (guided open-vehicle drives, off-road leopard tracking) instead of the rest camps, about $450-1,000 pppn in December. · Fare and schedule data are estimates. Exact-date December fares for TK, Airlink and KQ were not visible online, and the Airlink times come from flight trackers, not a published timetable. The SANParks 2026/27 conservation fee (from Nov 1 2026) is published in a PDF, but the figure could not be read; assume about 5-10% above R602.

### Then Kenya (Wild loop)
- **Route (one camping crew, all road):** Nairobi → Ol Pejeta 2n → **Samburu 3n** (NYE) → Thomson's Falls 1n → Lake Nakuru 2n → **Kakamega rainforest 2n** → Kericho 1n → **Mara conservancy 4n** → Naivasha + Hell's Gate 2n → airport hotel → fly home.
- **Exotic wildlife focus:** Samburu's Special Five + vulturine guineafowl, chimps + black rhino (Ol Pejeta), Rothschild's giraffe (Nakuru), colobus + De Brazza's monkeys + great blue turaco (Kakamega), big cats (Mara). See **Wildlife**.
- **No beach, no rental car:** crew 4x4 + driver-guide included.
- **Budget: ~$7,600 pp** (incl. flights + $300 contingency). Crew days are the cost driver.
- **Cuts:** skip Kakamega (−$800), home Jan 14 (−$450), yellow fever done (−$200), fly out of the Mara (−$90).
- **Fatigue:** max ~4.5h road/day, overnight stops split every long leg, 9 zero-travel days. Last day is a ~25h journey home.

itinerary.title: Depart LAX
itinerary.details: Sat evening. TK10 LAX about 19:45, about 13h to Istanbul. Sleep on the plane.

itinerary.title: Istanbul layover
itinerary.details: Land IST about 19:00. About 7h layover: lounge or airport hotel, shower, walk around. Board TK44 at 01:55.

itinerary.title: Arrive Cape Town, rest
itinerary.details: Land CPT 11:50. Pick up the rental car, 30 min drive to Gardens. Nap. Easy late afternoon at the V&A Waterfront or Bo-Kaap, or just sleep. Early night.

itinerary.title: Penguins + Cape Point
itinerary.details: Leave 07:30. 1.25h to Boulders: penguins before the crowds. Then Cape Point: bontebok, eland, ostrich, baboons, fynbos walk to the Cape of Good Hope. Back via Chapman's Peak, about 1.5h. Roughly 3h of driving in total, split.
itinerary.meals: Packed lunch (eat inside the car because of baboons); fish and chips at Kalk Bay or Hout Bay

itinerary.title: Table Mountain + Kirstenbosch
itinerary.details: Light day. Early cableway car if there is no wind (book online; a wind closure moves it to the afternoon). Dassies, views. Afternoon at Kirstenbosch (15 min drive): proteas and sugarbirds. Under 1h of driving. Pack for Kruger.
itinerary.meals: Self-cater breakfast; picnic at Kirstenbosch; dinner out

itinerary.title: Fly to Kruger, Christmas Eve
itinerary.details: Return the car at CPT. Airlink 4Z651 10:30 to Skukuza about 12:55. Pick up the Avis car and check in. 15:00-18:30 self-drive loop on the Sabie River (elephant, hippo, kudu). Optional SANParks sunset drive about 3h. Camp gates close about 18:30.
itinerary.meals: Plane snack; Skukuza restaurant; braai (barbecue) dinner

itinerary.title: Christmas on the Sabie River
itinerary.details: Gate opens 04:30. Dawn drive on H4-1 to Lower Sabie (43 km, 3-4h with stops, leopard country). Midday rest by the pool or river deck. Afternoon loop on S28 / H4-2 (rhino, lion, wild dog). Sunset at Sunset Dam. About 4-5h of slow game driving, broken into two sessions.
itinerary.meals: Packed breakfast; Christmas lunch at the camp restaurant; braai dinner

itinerary.title: Full Kruger day
itinerary.details: Optional SANParks morning walk (about 3-4h) OR a self-drive on H4-2 toward Crocodile Bridge and Gomondwane. Midday siesta through the heat and storms. Short late drive or SANParks night drive (civets, hyenas, bushbabies). Pack, and go to bed early.

itinerary.title: Kruger to Nairobi
itinerary.details: Leave 04:30-05:00. About 1h game drive on H4-2 to Crocodile Bridge gate, then about 1.5h on the N4 to MQP and drop off the car. Airlink 4Z840 10:50, JNB 11:45. Recheck your bags, then lunch with about 5h to spare. KQ763 17:00, about 4h, NBO 22:05. eTA check, 45 min transfer to Karen. Sleep.
itinerary.meals: Packed breakfast; JNB lunch; dinner on plane

itinerary.title: Land + rest day
itinerary.details: Wake at the guesthouse (landed last night). Rest. Optional: Sheldrick baby elephants 11:00 ($20, ~20m away; book online now).

itinerary.title: Drive north to Ol Pejeta
itinerary.details: Crew pickup ~08:30. ~4h via Nanyuki, equator stop. Camp set at OPC campsite. PM: chimp sanctuary + sunset drive.

itinerary.title: Rhinos + Mt Kenya
itinerary.details: Zero travel. Dawn + late drives. Black/white rhino, lion, elephant, Grevy's zebra. Optional lion tracking (~$70; not budgeted).

itinerary.title: North to Samburu + NYE by the river
itinerary.details: ~2.5–3h via Nanyuki + Isiolo; drop into hot, dry north. Camp on the Ewaso Ng'iro river. PM drive. Quiet NYE under the stars.

itinerary.title: Samburu Special Five
itinerary.details: Zero travel. Dawn + late drives: Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, gerenuk, Beisa oryx, Somali ostrich. Vulturine guineafowl, river elephants. Midday siesta (30–35°C).

itinerary.title: Leopards + river day
itinerary.details: Zero travel. Search riverine forest for leopard; lions, cheetah possible. Optional Samburu village visit (~$20–30 pp, paid locally).

itinerary.title: Back to the cool highlands
itinerary.details: ~3.5h via Isiolo + Nanyuki. Thomson's Falls (74 m) walk to the bottom. Camp at the falls; cool night (fleece).

itinerary.title: Short hop to Nakuru
itinerary.details: ~1.5h downhill to Lake Nakuru NP. Camp inside the park. PM drive: rhino, Rothschild's giraffe.

itinerary.title: Nakuru day
itinerary.details: Zero travel. Dawn drive to Baboon Cliff. Black + white rhino, flamingos/pelicans (numbers vary), tree-climbing lions if lucky. Siesta.

itinerary.title: West to the rainforest
itinerary.details: ~4–4.5h via Eldoret. Rondo Retreat inside the forest, full board. Dusk walk: colobus calling.

itinerary.title: Rainforest day
itinerary.details: Zero travel. Dawn bird walk with local guide (~Ksh300–500 pp): great blue turaco, hornbills. Black-and-white colobus, De Brazza's + red-tailed monkeys. Lirhanda Hill. Optional night walk (pottos, bushbabies).

itinerary.title: Tea country
itinerary.details: ~2.5–3h via Kisumu. Tea-estate walk, factory visit. Easy afternoon.

itinerary.title: Into the Mara conservancy
itinerary.details: ~3–3.5h via Bomet + Mulot (last hour rough). Camp in Enonkishu (or Pardamat/Ol Chorro). Dusk drive.

itinerary.title: Full Mara day
itinerary.details: Zero travel. Dawn + late drives, off-road, few vehicles. Big cats, plains game, newborn topi. Siesta.

itinerary.title: Maasai walk + night drive
itinerary.details: Zero travel. Morning walk with Maasai ranger. PM drive. Night drive if allowed (aardvark, bat-eared fox, genets).

itinerary.title: Extra Mara day
itinerary.details: Zero travel. Full-day drive with picnic lunch, following whatever the guides found. Sundowner.

itinerary.title: Road to Naivasha
itinerary.details: ~4–4.5h via Narok + Mai Mahiu. Lakeshore camp. Hippos at dusk.

itinerary.title: Hell's Gate + boat
itinerary.details: No long travel (30m local). Bike or walk Hell's Gate among zebra + giraffe, gorge hike. PM boat + Crescent Island walk. Rest.

itinerary.title: Airport hotel
itinerary.details: ~2.5–3h via A104 + Southern Bypass. Tip crew. Shower, repack, early night.

itinerary.title: Fly home
itinerary.details: Wake ~02:45, 10–20m to JKIA. TK608 04:50 → IST 11:45. ~2h45 airside connect. TK9 ~14:30 → LAX ~18:15 same day. ~25h door to door.

lodging.name: Once in Cape Town (private en-suite double)
lodging.includes: Private room with bathroom, Wi-Fi, breakfast (often included or optional), on-site parking
lodging.why: Safe, walkable street with restaurants and Uber everywhere, 10 min to the cableway and Kirstenbosch, 25-30 min to the airport. One of the cheapest decent private rooms in the city in peak season.
lodging.alternatives: Ashanti Lodge Gardens; Never@Home Green Point; or a Muizenberg / Kalk Bay guesthouse or Airbnb (closer to the penguins, about R1,800-2,500 per night)

lodging.name: Skukuza Rest Camp (bungalow BD2/BA2)
lodging.includes: En-suite double with fridge and AC, outdoor braai stand. Conservation fee is extra (R602 pp per day through Oct 2026; the 2026/27 rate applies from Nov 1).
lodging.why: 10 min from the Skukuza airport drop-off, on the river, restaurant and shop, sunset drives leave from camp. Lets you start Kruger the moment you land.
lodging.alternatives: Safari tent at Skukuza (cheaper, about R1,300-1,600 per tent); or guesthouses in Hazyview outside Paul Kruger gate

lodging.name: Lower Sabie Rest Camp (bungalow, river view if possible)
lodging.includes: En-suite double with AC and fridge, deck over the Sabie River in river units. Restaurant and pool in camp. Conservation fee extra.
lodging.why: Arguably the best camp for game density (rhino, lion, wild dog, elephant, hippo on the dam). A good place to spend Christmas, and the closest major camp to Crocodile Bridge gate for the Dec 27 exit.
lodging.alternatives: Crocodile Bridge camp; Marloth Park or Komatipoort guesthouses just outside Crocodile Bridge gate (about R1,400-2,000 per room) if SANParks is full. Both are even closer to the N4 for the drive to MQP.

lodging.name: Budget guesthouse near JKIA / Langata
lodging.includes: ~$60/room/night. Held from Dec 27 so it's ready at 03:30 Dec 28 (2 room-nights).
lodging.why: Cheap, safe, ~20m from Sheldrick + JKIA. Crew picks up here.

lodging.name: Operator camp at an OPC campsite
lodging.includes: OPC campsite $70 pppn (2026 tariff); entry separate
lodging.why: Cheapest way to sleep inside OPC.

lodging.name: Operator camp at a Samburu / Buffalo Springs campsite
lodging.includes: Campsite ~$20–50 pppn (public vs special site); reserve fee separate
lodging.why: Wake up on the Ewaso Ng'iro river among the Special Five.

lodging.name: Thomson's Falls campsite
lodging.includes: Campsite fee; operator tents, cook, meals
lodging.why: Splits Samburu → Nakuru into two easy days. Waterfall at the door.
lodging.alternatives: Thomson's Falls Lodge rooms ~$50–70 pp B&B

lodging.name: KWS public campsite inside Lake Nakuru NP
lodging.includes: KWS campsite $30 pppn; 2×24h park fee separate
lodging.why: Wake up inside the park. NYE by the fire.
lodging.alternatives: Flamingo Hill tented camp (~$150–185 pp FB)

lodging.name: Rondo Retreat
lodging.why: Only comfortable bed inside the rainforest. Guides at the gate.

lodging.name: Budget hotel, Kericho
lodging.why: Breaks Kakamega → Mara into two short drives.

lodging.name: Operator camp, Enonkishu conservancy (Pardamat/Ol Chorro fallback)
lodging.includes: Site/community fee ~$25 pppn est. Conservancy fee (~$80) separate.
lodging.why: Conservancy: few vehicles, walks, off-road. Confirm mobile camping in writing.

lodging.name: Camp Carnelley's or Fisherman's Camp
lodging.includes: Campsite fee; operator tents, cook, meals
lodging.why: Soft finish: Hell's Gate + boat day, 2.5–3h from the airport.

budget.notes: Aggregators show about EUR 380-430 round trip. One-way peak fare is an estimate. 20 kg checked bag on standard fares.

budget.item: Regional flights: Airlink MQP (Nelspruit) to JNB (4Z840, Dec 27)
budget.notes: Replaces Skukuza-JNB, whose 13:35 and 14:35 departures are too tight for KQ763. A busier route than Skukuza with several daily flights. Separate ticket from KQ.

budget.notes: Cape Point about R515 intl, Boulders about R190, cableway return about R495 (book online), Kirstenbosch about R250. Card only at SANParks gates.

budget.item: Tours/transport: Rental car Skukuza airport to MQP one-way, 3 days + fuel + drop fee

budget.notes: Sunset or night drive about R550-600, morning walk about R800-900. Book with the camp reservation.

practical:
## South Africa stopover
- **Visa (US passport):** US passport: visa-free for up to 90 days. You need 2 blank visa pages and 30+ days of passport validity after departure (bring 6 months to be safe). No yellow fever certificate is needed arriving from the US. Kenya eTA as already planned.
- **Safety — US State Dept Level 2: Exercise Increased Caution (issued May 27 2025, still Level 2 per reports as of Mar 2026; re-check travel.state.gov):** The advisory cites crime, terrorism, unrest and kidnapping. In practice the main risk for tourists is violent crime (robbery, carjacking, smash-and-grab, mugging) in city centers, at traffic lights and on some highways after dark. The places on this route (Gardens/City Bowl, the Cape Peninsula drive, Kruger camps, the N4 to Nelspruit in daylight, airports) are routine for tourists and low risk if you follow the usual precautions. Inside Kruger the main hazards are wildlife, speeding and heat, not crime. Southern Kruger is a low-to-moderate malaria area in summer.
  - Do not drive after dark outside the park, and keep to Kruger gate times (fines for late arrival).
  - Leave nothing visible in the car, lock the doors, and keep windows up at traffic lights (smash-and-grab).
  - Use Uber, not walking, in Cape Town after dark. Avoid the CBD and Long St late at night.
  - Use ATMs inside malls or the airport only, and shield your PIN.
  - At Cape Point and Boulders, carry no food in the open and keep car windows shut (baboons).
  - In Kruger, stay in the vehicle except at designated spots. Walks and night drives only with SANParks guides.
  - Take malaria prophylaxis for Kruger (December is rainy season), which you need for Kenya anyway, plus DEET and long sleeves at dusk.
  - Table Mountain: check that the cableway is running (it closes in wind), and don't hike alone.
  - Dec 27: drive the N4 from Komatipoort to Nelspruit in daylight only, without stopping at roadside spots. Airlink and KQ are on separate tickets, so keep the 5h buffer at JNB.
- **Weather in late Dec:** Cape Town is in peak summer: dry and sunny, about 16-27 C, often very windy (the southeasterly 'Cape Doctor', which can close the Table Mountain cableway), and light until about 20:00. Kruger is in its wet season: hot (about 20-33 C, sometimes 38 C+), green and lush, with afternoon thunderstorms. It is baby-animal season (impala lambs) with excellent birding, but wildlife is a bit more spread out than in the dry season.

## Entry
- Kenya eTA $30, **etas.gov.ke only**. Türkiye: airside connections only, no visa needed. Passport 6+ mo, 2 blank pages.

## Flights
- TK10 19:45→19:00+1. TK607 **20:30 → 03:05**. 1.5h connect: tight. Missed → next night; Ol Pejeta 1n shorter.
- Return Jan 16: TK608 04:50 → IST 11:45, ~2h45 airside connect, TK9 ~14:30 → LAX ~18:15. Check times when booking; keep ≥2h connect.

## Do we need a rental car? No.
- Safari days: the camping operator's 4x4 + driver-guide is in the crew price. You never drive.
- Self-drive is possible (e.g. Roadtrip Africa Land Cruisers + rooftop tent), but **Mara conservancies don't allow self-drive vehicles**, you'd do every 4–5h drive yourselves on the left, and an 8-day self-drive package starts ~€1,730 pp: not cheaper.
- Nairobi: Uber/Bolt. Everything else in the crew vehicle.

## Road reality
- Longest days: Dec 29 (~4h), Jan 6 (4–4.5h), Jan 13 (4–4.5h). Rest day before each.
- Samburu → Nakuru and Kakamega → Mara are split with overnights (Thomson's Falls, Kericho).
- Kericho → Mara via Mulot: last hour rough; ask operator about rain.

## Weather
- Samburu hot + dry (30–35°C days). Kakamega: afternoon showers, muddy trails: rain jacket + closed shoes. Highlands cold at night.


## Fees
- KWS Nakuru $90 new vs $60 old (court case). OPC + Mara conservancies not KWS. Cashless (card/M-Pesa).

## Operator must confirm in writing
- Mara conservancy mobile camping allowed + fee. Per-day rate incl. festive days. No hidden repositioning.

## Health (CDC)
- Yellow fever recommended outside Nairobi. Malaria pills from Dec 27 to 7 days after leaving Kenya (Kakamega/west is higher risk). DEET.

## Camping
- Walk-in tents, beds, bucket shower, toilet tent. Askari at night. Laikipia/Nakuru nights ~8–12°C: fleece.

## Money/safety
- ~130 KES/$. Crisp USD for tips. Kenya Level 2: Uber/Bolt, no night walks. Plastic bags banned.

label: South Africa: Cape + Kruger
summary: 3 nights on the Cape Peninsula (penguins, fynbos, Table Mountain), then 3 nights self-driving in southern Kruger in SANParks rest camps. Christmas is in Kruger. On Dec 27 you exit via Nelspruit (MQP) and reach NBO at 22:05. Then the Wild loop.

prelude.advisory_level: US State Dept Level 2: Exercise Increased Caution (issued May 27 2025, still Level 2 per reports as of Mar 2026; re-check travel.state.gov)
prelude.safety_short: Violent crime is the real risk (carjacking, mugging), mostly in cities and after dark. The Cape route and Kruger are routine and low-risk with care.
prelude.verdict_short: This is the most varied and self-sufficient stopover.
prelude.safety: The advisory cites crime, terrorism, unrest and kidnapping. In practice the main risk for tourists is violent crime (robbery, carjacking, smash-and-grab, mugging) in city centers, at traffic lights and on some highways after dark. The places on this route (Gardens/City Bowl, the Cape Peninsula drive, Kruger camps, the N4 to Nelspruit in daylight, airports) are routine for tourists and low risk if you follow the usual precautions. Inside Kruger the main hazards are wildlife, speeding and heat, not crime. Southern Kruger is a low-to-moderate malaria area in summer.
prelude.visa: US passport: visa-free for up to 90 days. You need 2 blank visa pages and 30+ days of passport validity after departure (bring 6 months to be safe). No yellow fever certificate is needed arriving from the US. Kenya eTA as already planned.
prelude.weather: Cape Town is in peak summer: dry and sunny, about 16-27 C, often very windy (the southeasterly 'Cape Doctor', which can close the Table Mountain cableway), and light until about 20:00. Kruger is in its wet season: hot (about 20-33 C, sometimes 38 C+), green and lush, with afternoon thunderstorms. It is baby-animal season (impala lambs) with excellent birding, but wildlife is a bit more spread out than in the dry season.
prelude.verdict: This is the most varied and self-sufficient stopover. The Cape adds wildlife and scenery Kenya doesn't have (penguins, fur seals, fynbos), and Kruger adds rhino, wild dog and leopard on cheap self-drive. It is also the most expensive stopover: about +$2,400 pp over the base trip, driven by 3 extra regional flights at peak fares. Kruger also partly duplicates the 19-night Kenya safari, and December school holidays mean SANParks camps may already be full, so check availability before buying anything. Checked: (1) TK44's winter departure is 01:55, not 01:45, so the IST layover is about 7h. (2) The Dec 27 exit is reworked. Skukuza-JNB flights leave only at about 13:35 or 14:35, which gave a dangerously short connection to KQ763 at 17:00 on a separate ticket. The plan now drives Lower Sabie to Kruger Mpumalanga airport (MQP, about 2.5h) for the 10:50 Airlink flight to JNB, leaving a 5h+ buffer. (3) The KQ763 fare is raised to about $450 (recent one-way fares about $410-450). A one-way car drop fee is added. (4) The headline delta is corrected from +$2,000 to about +$2,400, because the line items already summed to more than +$2,000. (5) Kidnapping and terrorism are added to the advisory notes. KQ763 (17:00 to 22:05), TK44's arrival, Airlink 4Z651 (10:30), the R602 conservation fee and the Level 2 advisory were all confirmed.
